description:
Signal: cargo test --test fz2_cli fails on Enum fixtures. After the fz-k22.14/.18/.20 fold, the old Cranelift verifier failure is gone, but native_enum_take_positive_single_call_survives_reduction_yield now deterministically reaches runtime and aborts in fz_closure_get_capture_ref: capture index 1 reads raw tag ValueKind(0), word 0x2.

Root cause repaired by the folded work: executable/transport symbols preserve ActivationKey.arrow; capture groundings and callable entry identity now cross transport.

Remaining defect: the callable-entry identity is still paired with an incorrect closure capture layout on an Enum.take reducer construction. The user-owned regression test src/compiler2/drive_test.rs::compiler2_native_enum_take_closure_constructors_match_entry_capture_counts is present in the integration worktree and must be preserved. Diagnose constructor capture lanes, selected callable entry capture_count, and codegen closure capture loading as one physical contract; do not introduce runtime fallback/reselection.

Goal: restore JIT and AOT execution for the existing fz2 Enum fixture contracts without suppressing diagnostics or relaxing the CLI tests.

Verification: enum_take_positive_single, enum_take_drop_split, and enum_predicate_search run/build; the constructor capture-count test; cargo test --test fz2_cli; cargo test --lib; strict clippy.

comments.text: fz-k22.20 deletion audit: `enum_take_drop_split` reaches a source publication position for CallableId(19) with BoundaryIds(4,5), but BoundaryId(4) still owns two concrete entries (targets 162/163) with the same physical ABI. Native now correctly refuses to invent a code pointer. The missing fact is upstream: publication must carry one exact callable-entry identity, or semantic/transport must split this pooled multi-specialization value before packaging. No native fallback or target/type re-selection remains.

title: Repair native Enum callable ABI regressions exposed by fz2 CLI
